part.text:
Done. The implementation is in `dominoes.go`:

- **`Domino`** is defined as `[2]int`, matching how the tests construct and compare dominoes.
- **`MakeChain`** uses a backtracking search: it tries each unused domino as the chain start (in either orientation), then repeatedly extends the chain with any unused domino whose left or right half matches the current end, flipping it when needed. The search is complete — it backtracks when a partial chain dead-ends — so it handles the "need backtrack" case where a greedy choice would fail. A finished chain is accepted only if it closes (`chain[0][0] == chain[len-1][1]`).
- Edge cases: empty input returns an empty chain (`true`), and a singleton is valid only if both halves match (returned unflipped, since the test requires exact equality for single-element chains).

Verification:
- `go test ./...` — all tests pass.
- `go test -bench BenchmarkMakeChain` — ~1.6µs/op across all cases, so the benchmark is fast too.

No files were created or modified other than `dominoes.go`; the test files are untouched.
